proposal.hypothesis: A 256-thread grid-stride kernel with a nominal 4096 elements per CTA and a 768-CTA cap tests an intermediate aggregation point between the measured 2048/1024 and 8192/512 configurations. At n=2^22, the cap yields 768 CTAs and about 5462 values per CTA; this may balance memory parallelism and atomic contention better, but the existing measurements do not isolate those factors.

retained: For n >= 1<<20, use a separate one-thread output-zeroing kernel followed by a multi-CTA grid-stride reduction in the same default stream.
Use 256-thread CTAs, ceil(n/4096) CTAs capped at 768, a warp/shared-memory block reduction, and one int32 atomicAdd per CTA.
Preserve the hierarchical reduction for positive sizes below the threshold; explicitly zero output for n <= 0.
